title: 1 in 4 Japanese Think AI Will Replace Friends
paragraphs: Can a computer be your friend? According to a new survey, about one in four people in Japan think that AI may one day take the place of friends and family.

The survey was carried out by the Japanese news agency Jiji Press. In June 2026, the agency asked 2,000 people aged 18 and older across Japan about their lives and communication. People were interviewed in person over four days, and 57.1% of them gave valid answers.
One question asked if people thought more advanced AI would replace their friends and family in the future. In total, 24.9% said yes, and 65.1% said no.

Younger people were more likely to say yes. Among people aged 18 to 29, 32.5% thought AI would replace friends and family. The number was 30.1% for people in their 30s, 29.2% for people in their 40s and 31.4% for people in their 50s.

The survey also asked about generative AI, such as ChatGPT. Overall, 30.8% of people said they used it, and 67.8% said they did not. Again, there were big differences between age groups. More than half of people in their 20s and 30s used generative AI. However, only 21.9% of people in their 60s used it.

People who used generative AI were also asked what they used it for, and they could choose more than one answer. The most common answer was work, at 64.7%. Next came housework, such as cleaning and cooking, at 35.3%. Then came asking about the news, at 27.1%. In addition, 21.7% said they chatted with AI about their favorite music, characters or famous people. And 12.8% said they told AI about their problems with love or work.
